questions.q: Why were the people of Jesus’ home town shocked about him?
questions.a: The people did not know from where he got his teachings, his wisdom, and his miracles.

questions.q: Where did Jesus say a prophet is without honor?
questions.a: Jesus said a prophet is without honor in his home town, among his relatives, and in his own household.

questions.q: What amazed Jesus about the people in his home town?
questions.a: Jesus was amazed by the unbelief of the people in his home town.

questions.q: What authority did Jesus give the Twelve as he sent them out?
questions.a: Jesus gave the Twelve authority over unclean spirits.

questions.q: What did the Twelve take with them on their journey?
questions.a: The Twelve took a staff, sandals, and one tunic.

questions.q: What did Jesus tell the Twelve to do if a place did not receive them?
questions.a: Jesus told the Twelve to shake off the dust under their feet as a testimony against them.

questions.q: Who did the people suppose Jesus was?
questions.a: The people supposed that Jesus was John the Baptizer or Elijah or a prophet.

questions.q: What had John the Baptizer told Herod he was doing unlawfully?
questions.a: John had told Herod it was unlawful for Herod to marry his brother’s wife.

questions.q: How did Herod react when he heard John preach?
questions.a: Herod became upset when he heard John preach, but he was still glad to hear him.

questions.q: What oath did Herod swear to Herodias?
questions.a: Herod swore that she could have whatever she asked of him, up to half of his kingdom.

questions.q: For what did Herodias ask?
questions.a: Herodias asked for the head of John the Baptizer on a platter.

questions.q: How did Herod react to Herodias’ request?
questions.a: Herod became very sorry but did not refuse her request, because of the oaths he had made in front of his guests.

questions.q: What happened when Jesus and the apostles tried to go away by themselves to rest?
questions.a: Many people recognized them and ran to arrive there before Jesus and the apostles.

questions.q: What was Jesus’ attitude toward the crowd that was waiting for them?
questions.a: Jesus had compassion on them because they were like sheep without a shepherd.

questions.q: When asked by Jesus, what did the disciples think they would have to do to feed the people?
questions.a: The disciples thought they would have to go and buy 200 denarii worth of bread.

questions.q: What food did the disciples already have with them?
questions.a: The disciples already had five loaves and two fish with them.

questions.q: What did Jesus do as he took the loaves and fish?
questions.a: As he took the loaves and fish, Jesus looked up to heaven, blessed and broke the loaves, and gave them to his disciples.

questions.q: How much food was left after everyone ate?
questions.a: There were 12 baskets of bread, and pieces of fish left after everyone ate.

questions.q: How many men had been fed?
questions.a: There were 5,000 men that had been fed.

questions.q: How did Jesus come to the disciples on the lake?
questions.a: Jesus came to the disciples walking on the lake.

questions.q: What did Jesus tell the disciples when they saw him?
questions.a: Jesus told the disciples to be brave and to not be afraid.

questions.q: Why did the disciples not understand about the miracle of the loaves?
questions.a: The disciples did not understand about the miracle of the loaves because their minds were slow to understand.

questions.q: What did the people of the region do when they recognized Jesus?
questions.a: The people brought the sick on stretchers to Jesus wherever they heard he was coming.

questions.q: What happened to those who just touched the fringe of Jesus’ garment?
questions.a: Those who just touched the fringe of Jesus’ garment were healed.

commentary.text: Christ despised in his own country.
John the Baptist put to death.
The apostles return, Five thousand fed by a miracle.
Christ walks on the sea, He heals those that touch him.

Verses 1–6 Our Lord's countrymen tried to prejudice the minds of people against him. Is not this the carpenter? Our Lord Jesus probably had worked in that business with his father. He thus put honour upon mechanics, and encouraged all persons who eat by the labour of their hands. It becomes the followers of Christ to content themselves with the satisfaction of doing good, although they are denied the praise of it. How much did these Nazarenes lose by obstinate prejudices against Jesus! May Divine grace deliver us from that unbelief, which renders Christ a savour of death, rather than of life to the soul. Let us, like our Master, go and teach cottages and peasants the way of salvation.

Though the apostles were conscious to themselves of great weakness, and expected no wordly advantage, yet, in obedience to their Master, and in dependence upon his strength, they went out. They did not amuse people with curious matters, but told them they must repent of their sins, and turn to God. The servants of Christ may hope to turn many from darkness unto God, and to heal souls by the power of the Holy Ghost.

Herod feared John while he lived, and feared him still more when he was dead. Herod did many of those things which John in his preaching taught him; but it is not enough to do many things, we must have respect to all the commandments. Herod respected John, till he touched him in his Herodias. Thus many love good preaching, if it keep far away from their beloved sin. But it is better that sinners persecute ministers now for faithfulness, than curse them eternally for unfaithfulness. The ways of God are unsearchable; but we may be sure he never can be at a loss to repay his servants for what they endure or lose for his sake. Death could not come so as to surprise this holy man; and the triumph of the wicked was short.

Let not ministers do any thing or teach any thing, but what they are willing should be told to their Lord. Christ notices the frights of some, and the toils of others of his disciples, and provides rest for those that are tired, and refuge for those that are terrified. The people sought the spiritual food of Christ's word, and then he took care that they should not want bodily food. If Christ and his disciples put up with mean things, surely we may. And this miracle shows that Christ came into the world, not only to restore, but to preserve and nourish spiritual life; in him there is enough for all that come. None are sent empty away from Christ but those who come to him full of themselves. Though Christ had bread enough at command, he teaches us not to waste any of God's bounties, remembering how many are in want. We may, some time, need the fragments that we now throw away.

The church is often like a ship at sea, tossed with tempests, and not comforted: we may have Christ for us, yet wind and tide against us; but it is a comfort to Christ's disciples in a storm, that their Master is in the heavenly mount, interceding for them. And no difficulties can hinder Christ's appearance for his people, when the set time is come. He silenced their fears, by making himself known to them. Our fears are soon satisfied, if our mistakes are set right, especially our mistakes as to Christ. Let the disciples have their Master with them, and all is well. It is for want of rightly understanding Christ's former works, that we view his present works as if there never were the like before. If Christ's ministers now could cure people's bodily diseases, what multitudes would flock after them! It is sad to think how much more most care about their bodies than about their souls.
